title: README examples for verify_chain and CrlChecker won't compile
description:
README.md contains code blocks marked ` ```rust ` (not no_run) that no longer
match the public API surface. Two examples won't compile:

1. README.md:65 — verify_chain with 5 arguments:

       let result = verify_chain(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &my_verifier, &NoRevocation)?;

   The current `verify_chain` signature (src/lib.rs:374) is 6 arguments;
   it takes `aia: &A` after `revocation`. The example needs a `&NoAiaFetcher`
   (or other `AiaFetcher`) tail argument. This was introduced by commit
   ec9bb744 / 50e43963 (Verifier 3rd generic for AiaFetcher) and not
   propagated to the README.

2. README.md:35-39, 45-47, 53-56 — CrlChecker::new() / with_delta() / OcspChecker::new()
   are bound directly:

       let checker = CrlChecker::new(crl_der, unix_now(), DefaultVerifier);
       let result = verify_chain_default(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &checker)?;

   `CrlChecker::new` and friends return `Result<Self>` (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs).
   Binding the Result and then passing `&checker` will not type-check
   — `&Result<CrlChecker>` does not implement `RevocationChecker`. The
   examples need either `.unwrap()`, `?`, or a `let checker = CrlChecker::new(...)?;`.

Both examples are in the README's primary onboarding flow; a new caller
copy-pasting them will hit cargo errors before they learn anything useful.

Suggested fix: add the README as a `#[doc = include_str!(\"../README.md\")]`
in lib.rs (or include the snippets directly) so `cargo test --doc` exercises
them; or convert the README to ```rust,ignore``` blocks. The former is
better — keeps the contract honest.

Caller impact: every new user.
close_reason:
Fixed, and the count was higher than filed: six of the eleven README examples did not compile, not two.

Item 1 (verify_chain with 5 args) was already STALE -- the README passes 6 including &NoAiaFetcher.

Item 2 (CrlChecker::new / OcspChecker::new bound as if infallible) was REAL and is fixed. Both return crate::Result<Self>, so &Result<CrlChecker> is not a RevocationChecker. The adjacent with_delta example already had its ?, which is how the inconsistency survived.

Four more the bead did not name, found by auditing every call against its signature: verify_tls_server, verify_tls_client_dns, verify_smime_signer, verify_code_signer and verify_time_stamper (five in total) all gained verifier and aia parameters. The README still passed a single &NoRevocation -- so besides being short two arguments, the argument it did pass sat in the VERIFIER position, teaching the wrong order. All now match: 8/8/8/7/7 arguments.

On the suggested fix: I tried #[doc = include_str!("../README.md")] and it does not work for this README. Every block is an illustrative fragment referencing chain/anchors/policy/crl_der that it never constructs, so doctesting them needs setup boilerplate inside a document whose purpose is to show call shape -- and #-hidden lines are not hidden on crates.io or GitHub, where this README is mainly read. Evidence: the experiment produced E0425 cannot-find-value for chain, anchors, policy, crl_der, delta_crl_der and unix_now across the blocks.

Guard instead: pkix-chain/tests/readme_examples.rs mirrors every README call argument for argument. Two directions, two mechanisms:
- a changed parameter list breaks compilation (verified: adding a parameter to verify_code_signer fails with "this function takes 8 arguments but 7 were supplied" plus the trait-bound errors)
- the README drifting away from the mirror fails every_readme_call_is_mirrored_here, which parses the calls out of README.md and requires each to appear in the mirror (verified: dropping arguments from the verify_tls_server example fails naming the stale call)

The second mechanism is the one that matters, because the failure mode here was a correct source and a stale document.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2344 tests.
